35: That they are effective against her will - that they serve to acquire in general: namely, intercourse [serves to acquire] a yevama, and a document in [the case of] divorce, and money in [the case of] a Hebrew maidservant.

In any event, with regard to marriage, we have not found [a case in which a woman can be acquired through] money against her will - which nevertheless, serves to acquire here [in the typical case of betrothal]. (And even against her will; if, for example, the father accepts betrothal [money] for a minor daughter... [Tosafot on Kiddushin:5a.14.1]) Thus: "Likewise, I will bring the mode of a wedding canopy..." [which generally effects acquisition, rendering a woman as married, and therefore it should also effect acquisition here.]
